title: Medical-Surgical Telemetry: adrenal (Addisonian) crisis in known Addison disease after viral gastroenteritis (24 h in 4-hour checkpoints)
diagnosis: Adrenal crisis in primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease): hypovolemic shock, hypoglycemia, hyponatremia 126, hyperkalemia 6.0 with peaked T waves, prerenal AKI; norovirus gastroenteritis
desc: Mon 0700 to Tue 0700 in seven 4-hour checkpoints: a 46-year-old teacher with Addison disease who vomited her hydrocortisone for 2 days arrives from the ED after hydrocortisone 100 mg IV and 2.5 L of fluid. Stress-dose hydrocortisone on time, a second low glucose, sodium correcting too fast (fluid change), positive then negative orthostatics, steroid insomnia and a night near-fall, falling potassium, then the oral taper, fludrocortisone restart and sick-day rules / emergency injection teaching. Includes an instructor guide with bedside-monitor settings and a debriefing.
